title: The strange business of Roman Abramovich

paragraphs: A new investigation shows how Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich hid his great wealth to avoid paying taxes.

Secret documents show that companies in Cyprus wrote fake and backdated papers for him. These papers helped hide over 600 million dollars worth of luxury items, including yachts, private planes, and expensive houses. The advisers also changed bank records, so Abramovich wouldn’t have to pay millions in taxes.

Today, Abramovich faces strict sanctions in many countries because of his close relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin. He can no longer do business in Britain, and his large superyachts are now parked in Turkey. Experts say changing official financial records to avoid taxes is against the law. Abramovich denies doing anything wrong and says he only followed advice from his financial team.

words.d: to stay away from something or prevent something bad from happening
to put an earlier date on an official document
an opinion given to help someone decide what to do

paragraphs: A new investigation has revealed that former Chelsea FC owner Roman Abramovich used fake, backdated financial documents to hide his wealth and avoid paying taxes.

The leak shows that Cyprus-based financial firms, along with major global accounting advisers, helped rewrite company records to secret away over 600 million dollars in luxury assets, including superyachts, private jets, and luxury homes. These firms also changed bank records to help the Russian oligarch avoid paying millions of dollars in local taxes on a 2 billion dollar fortune.

Since Russia invaded Ukraine, Abramovich has faced heavy international sanctions over his close ties to Vladimir Putin, which forced him to move his massive superyachts to safe waters in Turkey. While legal experts argue that these fake records amount to clear tax fraud that should face criminal prosecution, Abramovich’s legal team strongly denies any wrongdoing and insists he simply followed professional financial advice.

words.d: to hide or place something in a secret location so others cannot find or see it
a very rich and powerful business leader who often has strong connections to political leaders
the crime of tricking people or changing information to illegally get money or power

paragraphs: Roman Abramovich is a rich man from Russia. He owns Chelsea Football Club some time ago.

A new report shows that he uses fake papers to hide his money and pay less tax. Advisers help him hide big boats, planes, and expensive houses. These things cost hundreds of millions of dollars. Because he is a close friend of Russia’s president, many countries stop him from doing business there. Now, his big boats are in Turkey.
Experts say that hiding money with fake papers is a crime. Abramovich says that he does nothing wrong. He only does what his advisers tell him to do.

words.d: to put something in a place where others cannot see or find it
money which you must pay to the government
